q1.q: What is an AI health coach?
q1.a: It's an assistant you chat with that turns your health data into daily guidance. VITLS reads your wearable data (HRV, sleep, resting heart rate, weight, workouts), remembers your story and tells you what to do today across training, recovery, nutrition and body composition.

q2.q: Which wearables and apps does VITLS work with?
q2.a: VITLS will read live data from Garmin, Apple Health and Android Health Connect through its companion app, which is coming soon. Until then, you can tell the coach your weight, sleep, workouts and other numbers in the chat.

q3.q: How does VITLS decide whether I should train hard or rest?
q3.a: It compares your recent training load with your recovery signals (HRV, sleep and resting heart rate) against your own baseline. Then it tells you whether today is a day to push, keep it easy or recover.

q4.q: Why does my weight jump overnight, and can VITLS tell real fat change from noise?
q4.a: Day-to-day scale changes are mostly water, glycogen and food in transit, not fat. VITLS looks at your weight trend over time to separate short-term noise from a real change in body composition.

q5.q: Does VITLS remember things about me?
q5.a: Yes. It keeps the story you share, such as injuries, goals and life events, and uses it in later advice, so you don't have to explain yourself again.

q6.a: VITLS is launching on EU infrastructure, data travels encrypted, and sensitive records such as sleep stages, workouts and meal notes are encrypted with a key unique to your account. You can also bring your own AI key, so you control which AI provider processes your conversations.

q7.q: Is VITLS a replacement for a doctor?
q7.a: No. VITLS gives coaching, not medical advice. It does not diagnose or treat conditions; talk to a healthcare professional about medical concerns.

q8.q: How is VITLS different from wearables like WHOOP or Oura?
q8.a: WHOOP and Oura are wearables with their own apps. VITLS is not a device: it's a coach you chat with that uses data from wearables you already own, lets you choose a coaching style, and covers nutrition, training, recovery and long-term goals in one conversation.

q9.q: Does VITLS support people on GLP-1 medication?
q9.a: Yes. If your doctor has prescribed GLP-1 therapy such as semaglutide or tirzepatide, VITLS helps you hit protein, fluid and fiber targets, log symptoms and doses, and export a log for your doctor. It never advises on doses.

legal.title: Legal information and privacy
legal.metaDescription: Operator details and the privacy notice for the VITLS website (vitls.ai), run by VERTISPACE s.r.o., Brno.
operator: Registered in the Commercial Register kept by the Regional Court in Brno, section C, file 137480
sections: VERTISPACE s.r.o. (details above) is the controller of personal data processed through this website, vitls.ai. You can reach us at hey@vitls.ai.
This notice covers the marketing website vitls.ai. The VITLS app (app.vitls.ai), including the health data from your wearables, is covered by a separate privacy notice in the app.

To deliver the website, our hosting provider processes technical data: your IP address, the date and time, the page requested, and browser and device information. We use it only to run and secure the site (legitimate interest, Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR). We use no analytics, advertising trackers or third-party embeds; fonts and images are served from our own domain.

We set one cookie, NEXT_LOCALE, which remembers the language you chose for the current browser session. It is strictly necessary for that function, holds no personal identifier and is deleted when you close the browser. No other cookies or browser storage are used, so no consent banner is needed.
If you email us, we process your address and message to reply to you (Art. 6(1)(b) or (f) GDPR) and keep them only as long as the conversation and related legal obligations require.

The website is hosted by Vercel Inc. (USA) and our email runs on Google Workspace (Google). Where data leaves the EU/EEA, it is protected by the EU–US Data Privacy Framework and/or the European Commission's Standard Contractual Clauses.

You have the right to access, rectify, erase, restrict and port your data, and to object to processing. Write to hey@vitls.ai. You can also lodge a complaint with the Czech Office for Personal Data Protection (ÚOOÚ), Pplk. Sochora 27, 170 00 Prague 7, www.uoou.gov.cz.
We may update this notice when the website changes. The date above shows the current version.

chat.ask: Day 2 after my shot and I'm not hungry at all. What should I eat?
chat.answer: Small and protein first: a skyr and a handful of nuts gets you to 50 of 110 g. Sip water through the afternoon, you're at 0.8 of 2 litres. Last week nausea was worse after fatty dinners, so keep tonight light.

safety.title: Your doctor leads. VITLS keeps the log.
safety.body: VITLS is coaching and tracking, not medical advice. It never suggests or changes doses and never changes targets your clinician set. If you lose weight faster than about 1% a week, it points it out so you can raise it with your doctor.

q1.a: No. You can record your medication, injection day and every dose change your doctor makes, but VITLS never suggests, changes or comments on doses. Dose questions belong with your prescriber.

q2.q: Which GLP-1 medicines does it work with?
q2.a: Any GLP-1 or dual-agonist therapy you've been prescribed, for example semaglutide (Ozempic®, Wegovy®) or tirzepatide (Mounjaro®, Zepbound®). You choose the medicine and weekday in your profile. VITLS isn't affiliated with any manufacturer.

q3.q: Where do the protein, fluid and fiber targets come from?
q3.a: VITLS starts from commonly recommended daily values for people on GLP-1 therapy and asks you to confirm or edit them with your doctor. If your clinician has set targets, VITLS uses those and never changes them.

q4.q: Can VITLS stop me losing muscle?
q4.a: No app can promise that. VITLS helps you keep an eye on the factors you control, protein intake and strength training, and shows your lean-mass trend as reported by your smart scale or fitness platform.

q5.q: What can I share with my doctor?
q5.a: You can export your food intake, weight, symptoms (appetite, nausea, constipation) and logged doses for any date range as a CSV or PDF. VITLS is coaching, not medical advice; contact your doctor about any symptom that worries you.
